summary: Discord music autoplay no longer repeats the same few songs, starts the next track instantly instead of after a network gap, and survives a dropped voice connection without stranding a fake now-playing state.
details: Autoplay reseeds one-at-a-time from whatever just finished, and YouTube's Mix only ever excludes its own seed -- so a long autoplay chain drifted into repeating the same few tracks of one Mix neighborhood. MusicPlayer now keeps a session-scoped, in-memory set of locators that actually started playing (_played_locators). Autoplay's pick selection skips anything already in it and takes the next fresh track from the Mix; an all-repeats Mix falls through to idle exactly like an empty one. User-requested playback is never deduped.

Autoplay prewarm ([music] autoplay_prewarm_seconds, default 0): the next autoplay pick -- its Mix lookup AND its playable stream -- is resolved by a timer before the current track's expected end, so the track-end advance plays the prewarmed stream directly with zero network calls at the gap. Only armed for the last track in the queue; a stale or already-played prewarmed pick is discarded, never reused.

A dead voice connection no longer escapes into the on_finished handler and strands a fake now-playing state. Two defences, found live 2026-08-26: _advance catches a raising voice.play() and tears the session down like a stop (R-65, and the manager drops the dead player so a fresh /music play joins cleanly), and DiscordVoiceSession runs a voice-death monitor (R-66) that probes the voice websocket + audio thread every 5s while a track is loaded -- two consecutive dead observations (WS closed, or discord.py stopped claiming is_playing() while a source is still loaded) fire on_voice_death and tear the session down. A natural track end clears the loaded marker so the monitor never mistakes an ordinary idle queue for a dead connection. (Hardened per independent external audit, 2026-08-26.)

Music messages are now consistent: every surface (slash replies, now-playing controls, queue view, track-end and autoplay notifications) uses the same 'Now playing: {title} — {url}' format, 'Queued:' for added-to-queue, and the play_music agent tool reports a 'queued' flag when a track was queued behind another instead of claiming it is playing.
limitations: The played history is session-scoped and in-memory: a restart (or deploy) begins a fresh window, so a track played before a restart can be autoplayed again after it.
Prewarm is only as good as the track duration yt-dlp reported: a track far shorter than expected can outrun the prewarm timer and fall back to the old at-end lookup.
The Mix is still reseeded one track at a time from whatever most recently played -- a multi-track lookahead queue remains deferred.
